solutionSql:
WITH firsts AS (
  SELECT customer_id,
         date_trunc('month', MIN(booked_at) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS cohort_start
  FROM shipments
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
activity AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id,
         date_trunc('month', booked_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS month_start
  FROM shipments
)
SELECT to_char(f.cohort_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS cohort,
       COUNT(*) AS cohort_size,
       COUNT(a.customer_id) AS retained
FROM firsts AS f
LEFT JOIN activity AS a
  ON a.customer_id = f.customer_id
 AND a.month_start = f.cohort_start + interval '1 month'
GROUP BY f.cohort_start
ORDER BY f.cohort_start;
ambiguities: The ticket does not say whether cancelled shipments count as a booking for retention. I counted all statuses.
'Following month' is read as exactly the cohort month plus one calendar month. A customer who booked two months later but not in the next month is not retained.
Customers with no shipments have no cohort and are excluded. The ticket implies this without saying it.
The cohort_size and retained columns are bigint, and the ticket names no types.
notes: Each named dataset returned one cohort (2025-12) with retained equal to cohort_size (6 in the sample). Every cohort member also booked in January, so the outputs do not separate the next-month rule from a same-month rule (which would also return 6) or an any-later-month rule. The retention rule itself is not exercised by these datasets.
